name: Invest Bank
founded: 1975 (Emiri Decree of the Ruler of Sharjah No. 153/02/1975; formerly Invest Bank for Trade and Finance)
ownership_summary: Government-controlled after two rescues. The Government of Sharjah took 50.07% in 2019 (1,592,857,143 new shares at AED 0.7, approved by the AGM on 10 Apr 2019) and then recapitalised the bank under a plan approved by the EGM on 27 Apr 2023. That plan comprised an AED 2.6bn rights issue, which took share capital to AED 3.2bn in about 263bn shares of AED 0.0121684 nominal, plus a Government of Sharjah guarantee over legacy assets (originally AED 3.0bn, reduced to AED 1.26bn in H1 2026). Capital Intelligence (Oct 2026) says the Government of Sharjah owns 88% directly and indirectly; Argaam (Oct 2025) gives about 70% Government of Sharjah and 18% Sharjah Social Security Fund. An EGM on 15 Oct 2026 votes on a 1-for-82.18 share consolidation back to AED 1 nominal, with capital unchanged at AED 3.2bn.

shareholders.holder: Government of Sharjah, direct and indirect combined (per Capital Intelligence)

government_link: Yes — the Government of Sharjah owns 88% directly and indirectly (Capital Intelligence, 7 Oct 2026). It is the 'ultimate controlling party' and gives a special guarantee covering legacy-asset losses (AED 1.26bn remaining in H1 2026).
group_structure: Single listed bank. No subsidiaries identified from accessible sources. An Islamic banking window was approved by the CBUAE in Oct 2025 under the brand 'Invest Bank – Islamic'. Legacy problem assets from the pre-2019 private-ownership era are covered by provisions and the Government of Sharjah guarantee.
footprint: UAE; head office Sharjah. Branch count not verified (bank website blocked).
customer_segments: Large corporates, conglomerates, government and GREs, banks and high-net-worth individuals (drivers of 2025 loan growth per Capital Intelligence). Retail and SME banking built from a negligible base over about 18 months to Q2 2026, with retail lending so far fully secured.
business_lines: Corporate banking, retail banking (DigiBank mobile app launched 2025), SME banking, treasury and investments, Islamic window ('Invest Bank – Islamic', licensed Oct 2025). Detailed segment data not accessed.

capabilities.wealth_summary: No evidence of a wealth, private-banking or investment offer was found, but the bank's own website (inb.ae) and ADX disclosures were blocked (HTTP 403), so the product range could not be checked directly. Invest Bank is a Sharjah government-controlled turnaround: recapitalised in 2023 (AED 2.6bn rights issue plus a legacy-asset guarantee), new management since Sep 2024, and back in profit in 2025. Per Capital Intelligence (Oct 2026), retail and SME businesses 'did not exist in any meaningful form 18 months ago' and now contribute materially to operating income; 2025 loan growth included high-net-worth individuals; the bank is investing heavily in technology, staffing and franchise development. In 2025 it launched the DigiBank mobile app, joined the Aani instant-payment platform and won CBUAE approval for an Islamic window ('Invest Bank – Islamic'). A three-year strategy ('Midaf') was launched in Q4 2025, focused on digital transformation.

private_banking.detail: No private banking unit found in accessible sources; Capital Intelligence notes lending to high-net-worth individuals in 2025. Website not accessible.

digital_investing.detail: DigiBank mobile banking app launched in 2025 (with Aani instant payments); no evidence on investment features (website and app store pages not checked).

initiatives.what: Government of Sharjah became 50.07% shareholder (1,592,857,143 new shares at AED 0.7 per share, AED 1.1bn); capital rose to AED 3.2bn at the time

EGM approved recapitalisation plan: AED 2.6bn rights issue (capital AED 3.2bn, ~263bn shares at AED 0.0121684) and Government of Sharjah guarantee over legacy assets; CAR rose from 2.77% (end-2022) to 38.6% (end-2023)
Received AED 0.5bn under the Sharjah guarantee; implemented a cloud-based core banking solution
Vice Chairman Idris Al Rafi took over as CEO and rebuilt the management team
Launched DigiBank mobile banking app and registered on Aani instant payments; first net profit in eight years (about AED 0.2bn); accumulated losses down to AED 1.5bn (48.57% of capital)
CBUAE approved Islamic banking window, to operate as 'Invest Bank – Islamic'
Launched three-year strategy 'Midaf' focused on core-business growth and digital transformation (Q4 2025)
General assembly amended the Articles of Association (published Sep 2026)
Capital Intelligence raised LT FCR to BBB+ (from BBB-), citing franchise development by new management and retail/SME growth
EGM to vote on 1-for-82.18 share consolidation restoring AED 1 nominal value (capital unchanged at AED 3.2bn)

opportunities: Retail and SME franchise being built from scratch since about 2025, with new DigiBank app and heavy investment in technology and franchise (S3, S1).
Loan growth includes high-net-worth individuals; new Islamic window licensed Oct 2025 (S3, S6).
Three-year 'Midaf' strategy (Q4 2025) puts digital transformation first; cloud-based core banking implemented in 2024 (S1).
barriers: Still a turnaround: accumulated losses AED 1.5bn (48.57% of capital) at end-2025; NPLs 28% of gross loans (fully provided) in Jun 2026; high cost-to-income ratio and declining capital ratios (S1, S3).
Small balance sheet (about AED 16bn assets) with heavy customer and real-estate concentration (S8, S3).
No evidence of any wealth or investment proposition (website not accessible to confirm).
